verdict: Lend selectively to asset-backed Siliguri transport and warehousing operators with clean receivables; hold off on thin-margin, high-capex warehousing builds until the ₹200 crore state plan converts into named projects and tenants.
title: Siliguri logistics & warehousing: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**A Siliguri logistics borrower moves goods, not promises: trucks, godowns, cold rooms and handling equipment turn diesel, rent, driver wages and loading labour into freight and storage revenue.** Cash arrives from traders, FMCG and pharma distributors, and e-commerce feeders; it leaves upfront for fuel, driver advances and rent. **The value sits in the route and the shed, not the balance sheet** — a trucker's pricing power is thin and set by the load, while a warehousing operator earns from occupancy and contract tenure. **So when a proposal lands, check whether the borrower owns the asset or merely rents capacity; if rented, ask who holds the lease and for how long.**

## What has changed now
**Two local facts matter and both are fresh.** NFR has opened the 6.8-km Rangapani-Bagdogra siding line for regular freight, removing the reversal at Siliguri Junction and expecting at least 10 freight trains daily from ECR at Forbesganj [1]. Separately, the state budget earmarked ₹200 crore to develop Siliguri as a logistics and trade hub through integrated logistic parks, multi-modal transport, modern warehousing and cold-chain [2][3]. **These are announcements and rail operations, not yet signed tenant contracts** — treat the ₹200 crore as a pipeline signal, not collateral. **When a proposal cites the hub plan, ask for the specific park, allotment letter or anchor tenant; if none exists, underwrite on today's cash flows only.**

## Where the growth is
**Peer results show the demand is real at the organised end.** Delhivery's Q2 FY27 service revenue was ₹3,066 crore, up 19.8% year-on-year, with express parcel shipments at 325 million, up 32.1% [4][5][6]. VRL Logistics reported Q1 FY27 revenue growth of 18% with EBITDA margin at 21.8% and full-year volume growth guided at 8% [7]. **Pursue the small operator who feeds these networks** — last-mile fleet owners with 5-25 trucks on contract, cold-chain handlers serving pharma and agri, and shed owners with a named tenant. **Avoid the speculative godown builder with no tenant and the pure-spot trucker with no contract book.**

## How to grow safely
**Structure against the asset and the receivable, not the story.** Rating evidence shows the risk clearly: Pranik Logistics' working cycle stretched from 39 days in FY23 to 77 days in FY24 as collection period moved from 52 to 82 days [11]. **So take monthly stock and receivable statements, and set a covenant that collection days do not cross the sanctioned cycle; if they do, ask for the ageing and stop fresh limits.** For capex-heavy borrowers, note that Tara Chand carried interest coverage of 11 times and net cash accrual to adjusted debt of 0.6 times in fiscal 2025 despite continuing high capex [8], while an earlier ICRA note on the same name showed DSCR near 1.0 times over three years on debt-funded capex [9] — old, 2023, but the lesson holds. **Take every month: fuel and toll spend, fleet utilisation, tenant rent receipts, and a stock-and-receivables statement.**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the cash conversion, not the turnover.** A borrower whose collection period drifts past the sanctioned cycle, or who funds new sheds from working capital, is the one to exit. **If diesel and driver costs rise while freight rates stay flat, ask for the rate card and the contract tenure.** If a borrower's only answer to the hub plan is a newspaper clipping, decline. **Siliguri-specific published data is thin — the sources here are local news and national peers, so lean on first principles and the borrower's own numbers.**
watch: Collection days cross the sanctioned cycle -> freeze fresh limits and seek ageing
Utilisation falls while fuel spend holds -> ask for rate card and contract tenure
Rent receipts lapse or tenant exits -> re-underwrite on vacant-shed cash flow
Capex funded from working capital -> restructure to term loan or decline
Volumes fall below the 10-train expectation [1] -> reassess feeder-route exposure
watch_note: Trigger levels are policy suggestions (analytical framing), not data.
